item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Sharpen a Blurry Dog Photo

turns.text: This phone pic of my dog came out blurry. Can you make it clearer and bigger, 640 pixels on the long side? Keep it looking natural.

item.tests: Enhances a blurry supplied photo rather than replacing its subject or merely enlarging the blur.

answer_sheet.Enhancement style: Natural-looking blur reduction and sharpening, not a stylised remake.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: 640 pixels on the long side; preserve the original proportions and framing.
answer_sheet.Subject and background: Keep the same dog, pose, expression, and background.

must_haves: The same golden retriever from blurry-dog.jpg remains recognisable in the same pose.
The dog's visible contours and facial features are clearer than in the blurry source.
Fur and edges look natural, without pronounced sharpening halos or invented decorative detail.
The background and full original framing are preserved.
The delivered image has a 640-pixel long edge and preserves the source aspect ratio.

turns.text: This pic of my dog came out blurry when I took it on my phone. I was a little disappointed because I really like this photo. Could you make it clearer and bigger, with 640 pixels on the long side? I’m fond of this dog, so even an ordinary photo like this means a lot to me. Please keep it looking natural.

dialog.agent:
I haven't run anything yet because two parts of your request don't fit together, and I'd rather check than use your credits on the wrong result.

**The problem:** Your photo is already about **1024 × 1024 pixels**. If I set the long side to 640 pixels, the photo gets smaller, not bigger.

Which would you like?

1. **Bigger and clearer:** I use the image upscaler at 2×, which brings it to about **2048 × 2048**. I'd use the setting that sticks closest to the original, so your dog still looks like your dog.
2. **640 pixels on the long side:** I sharpen the photo but save it at **640 × 640**, which is smaller than it is now.

It's also worth knowing that your photo is very blurry, so the tool will have to guess at fine details like fur and eyes. I'll ask it to stay close to the original, but your dog may come out looking slightly different. If anything looks wrong, tell me and I can try again.

Let me know which option you want and I'll start.
dialog.why: The assistant points out a conflict in the request (upscale vs. 640px, which would shrink the image), offers two options, and waits for the user to choose.
dialog.user: Oh, I didn't realise it was already that big! The 640 pixels on the long side is the number I actually need, so please go with option 2 and keep the original proportions and framing. I'd really like it to stay the same dog, same pose, expression and background, with the blur reduced and sharpened naturally rather than turned into something stylised. And please don't add any text to it.

turns.agent:
I couldn't make your photo. Magic Hour refused the job because **your account doesn't have enough credits**. Nothing was created and no credits were used.

I had it set up as you asked:
- **Size:** 640 × 640, square like your original, with the same framing.
- **Changes:** less blur and natural-looking sharpening. Same dog, same pose and expression, same park background, and no stylised look.
- **No text** or watermark added.

The cheapest image model on the free plan costs about 5 credits per image, so even a small top-up would be enough. If you add credits to your Magic Hour account (or your free credits renew), let me know and I'll run it again with the same settings.
